Subject: Onboarding questions and short pilot — PO requirement?

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at SprinterTech is excited to trial Redwood for our internal search assistant. Before we start the two-week pilot we need to confirm procurement steps.

Our procurement policy mandates a purchase order for all vendor spend, which is going to slow the kickoff by ~2 weeks with our legal and AP routing. Is there any path to begin a short trial without a formal PO in place? We can provide a signed workorder or an internal approval memo if that helps.

We anticipate spend under $3,000 for the pilot period. If a formal waiver is needed, what evidence or assurances do you require (SLA, data handling, invoice cadence)?

Appreciate the guidance.

Best,
Emily
Emily Tran
Head of Platform Operations, SprinterTech
Attachment: SprinterTech_Onboarding_Form.pdf (PDF)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Onboarding questions and short pilot — PO requirement?

Marissa / Laura — forwarding Sprinter's ask. They want to start a 2-week pilot but procurement wants a PO which will delay kickoff. SprinterTech expects <$3k spend.

Questions for adjudication:
- Can we approve a temporary PO waiver for pilots under $5k for strategic prospects (sales-approved)?
- What evidence do we require from the customer (signed workorder, SSO config confirmation, IP/data handling acknowledgement)?
- Should we issue a formal temporary waiver doc (temp-waiver-template.docx) and have PM/Sales countersign?

My recommendation: approve a one-off waiver for this pilot with the following controls: spend cap $5k, signed workorder, billing to start after pilot (invoice only), and a 30-day evidence retention entry in our onboarding tracker. This preserves our procurement guardrails but keeps the momentum.

I can own the external comms if you greenlight.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher

Thanks Sean — quick thoughts from procurement side: we do have precedent for short-term exceptions for proof-of-concept work, but approvals should be kept tight. Proposed approval matrix for this case: 

- Threshold & duration: single pilot <= $5,000 and <= 30 days.
- Required customer artifacts: signed workorder or email authorization on company letterhead + onboarding form (they attached the form already).
- Internal approvals: Sales director (Sean) + Finance ops (Laura) sign the temporary waiver.
- Controls: tag deal in procurement tracker, restrict invoice net-30, do not enable auto-renew without PO.

I'll attach a fillable temporary-waiver-template.docx and a pre-filled waiver text you can send to SprinterTech. If you want, we can make the waiver revocable if any compliance red flags appear during the pilot.

Approve conditionally — send external language and I will countersign once the artifacts are back.

Marissa Cole

Emily — thanks for the quick follow-up. Good news: we've approved a limited, revocable waiver to let SprinterTech begin the two-week pilot without a formal PO. Summary of the agreed controls below (please confirm):

- Scope & cap: single pilot for Redwood hosted API access, capped at $5,000 total.
- Evidence needed: signed workorder or signed confirmation email on company letterhead (please attach). We received your onboarding form — thanks.
- Billing: we'll invoice after the pilot (net-30). No automatic renewal or subscription activation without a PO.
- Security/compliance: your SOC2 snapshot and the onboarding form are sufficient for this pilot; no additional data residency changes requested.
- Term: waiver valid for this pilot only (30 days) and is revocable if compliance issues arise.

Next steps: please reply with the signed workorder or an email approval from your procurement contact. I've attached the temporary waiver for countersignature and a DocuSign link if you prefer to sign electronically: https://docusign.com/link/abcdef123456

Looking forward to getting the pilot started this week.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
